criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: Refined 2026-11-10 after reading the road, seam, prop, water and structure jobs and the stores. (1) sim/state/city_view.h CityView: a struct of references a job-path function takes in place of const CityState& (catalog, roads, street, lots, lot_book, buildings, nature, damage, transit, the revisions, marking_style, clock) with terrain a GroundRead (the live Heightfield or a GroundPatch: final, natural and water samples of a window); CityData converts to it implicitly, so live callers (sim, api, main thread) compile unchanged. (2) sim/state/city_cut.h CityCut: owns partial stores of a box under their own ids and exposes a CityView of them; cut_city(s, box, parts) is the only place a job takes map_mutex (shared, for the copy). core/id_table.h IdTable<T> replaces std::vector for id-indexed tables (roads.nodes/segs, grade.prof/node, street runs, buildings.items, street tables, terrain.road_shapes): dense in the live city, sparse in a cut; an id a cut does not hold stops the debug DLL (core stop macro) and reads a dead record in release. SpatialHash gets a validity box in a cut: a query that leaves it stops the debug DLL. (3) Kept facts are resolved at gather, under the lock, from the live caches (furniture Spots of the box's segments, NodeShape of its nodes, SegWalls of its walled segments): the job is a pure function of its cut and writes no cache the simulation or a state-deriving reader reads (FurnitureKept, RoadShapes), so a cut can never poison the state. street_run's facts a job needs are stored per segment (StreetRun, and the row face moved into it at settle so lamp_row walks no street). (4) MeshQueueOf::submit_job(gather, build): the lock lives inside gather. MapRead (city_state.h) is the one shared-lock guard, counting depth per thread; MeshBuilder::add counts vertices added while the thread holds the map (debug DLL); probe map_hold. Failing check first: tests/core/map_hold_test (town streamed in: built_under_map == 0). (5) take_city leaves the session catalog in place (jobs read it by reference with no lock). Converted in order, each compiling and tested: roads, structures, far roads, water, seams (P10), props; then P33 cover and trees, P34 transit, P35 overlays; shore/canyon/fog/ecology/ruin jobs checked against the same probe. Test: a probe of the units made a frame (zero at rest, nothing pending), the streaming tests (camera_pan, chunk streams) unchanged in what is drawn.

title: Every MultiMesh instance (16 or 20 floats) is kept three more times on the CPU by the engine…
symptom: Every MultiMesh instance (16 or 20 floats) is kept three more times on the CPU by the engine besides the GPU buffer: 256 to 320 bytes an instance. (Process memory growing with the instances in reach (log/performance.md P-03; counts to total per family).)
cause: Everything that repeats (building part bands and bays, props, trees, cover, street furniture, agents) is drawn as MultiMesh instances, and Godot MultiMesh storage keeps its own copies.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: What multiplies the rows goes: a family has one MultiMesh whose shadow and level draws are instances of it (P13, P29, C7), and the copies the engine keeps are read first in the engine's source (servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/mesh_storage.cpp multimesh_allocate_data, multimesh_set_buffer: data_cache, previous buffers for interpolation, dirty regions) and in context7, then allocated so none the game does not use is kept. Check: memory_probe per instance before and after, props and trees photos equal.

title: MeshBuilder writes a vertex with five push_back calls on Godot Packed arrays and reads positions…
symptom: MeshBuilder writes a vertex with five push_back calls on Godot Packed arrays and reads positions back in tri(), each a call across the GDExtension boundary; a quad is four unshared vertices. (Slow mesh jobs: more worker CPU, and longer holds of the map shared (P-02).)
cause: The builder stores straight into the engine array types so the surface can be handed over without a copy; every road, prop, tree, water and agent job pays the boundary per vertex.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: MeshBuilder keeps its vertices in storage the core owns (one interleaved record a vertex in a std::vector grown by doubling: no engine call a vertex), tri() reads it; at bake render/surface_streams.cpp writes the engine's vertex, attribute and index bytes straight from it (one allocation each), with no Packed arrays in between; Shell writes through the same writer (P7). Check every reader of mb.v and mb.idx (ground_seam.cpp read_paving, MeshBuilder::bounds, mesh_levels, the agents' wrecks, far_road tag), surface_data.cpp. Test: shell_test, digest, road and building photos byte-equal, render_cost bytes.

title: A vehicle level is chosen by fixed radii (cabin_close_m, the tier cabin reach, far_radius_m); past…
symptom: A vehicle level is chosen by fixed radii (cabin_close_m, the tier cabin reach, far_radius_m); past far_radius_m every vehicle out to the 900 m publish radius draws the far mesh (666 to 1380 triangles each; 1.1 to 1.3 M triangles for some 1900 far vehicles in the round4 logs). (GPU vertex work every frame for cars a few pixels long, in the picture and again where they cast (log/performance.md P-06).)
cause: The fleet does not ask render/detail.h (the one owner of level of detail by screen error): there is no level below far and no cut by projected size.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: AgentRenderer::update asks render/detail.h (the one owner of level of detail by screen error) where a vehicle's far mesh falls under render.detail_error_px: past it the vehicle has no row in the main pass (its shadow stays the fleet's sector hull, fleet_shadow.h), so the far level ends by projected size and not by the publish radius. Where: agent_renderer.cpp level_of / plain_level and the far branch of the vehicles' loop; who else: draw_rows, FleetShadow::add, the parked cars' loop, agent_cost. Test: agent_cost's far instances from a far view fall to those above the error; quality_test; a far traffic photo with nothing missing at the size it shows.

title: Every vehicle draw and its shadow twin share one box of 1800 m round the camera, and the people 48…
symptom: Every vehicle draw and its shadow twin share one box of 1800 m round the camera, and the people 48 draws one of 560 m with shadows on for both mesh levels: the engine culls a MultiMesh whole, so each of the sun four cascades draws every casting instance of the disc. The seen rows are uploaded twice (the draw and, appended to the cast rows, its shadow MultiMesh). (GPU time in the shadow passes and main-thread upload time every frame (P-07).)
cause: Agents are drawn as camera-wide MultiMeshes refilled by hand, one per model and level, instead of in spatial cells the cascades can cull; a shadow level is a second MultiMesh with its own copy of the rows.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: the agents' casting rows go by spatial sector, as FleetShadow already does for the far level: a shadow draw a sector for the cabin and body levels (each sector's box its own, so a cascade culls the sectors it does not cover) in place of one camera-wide shadow MultiMesh a model and level; the people's draws the same. The rows the camera sees are written once and the sector's caster reads the same poses. Where: agent_renderer.cpp draw_rows and update (casts), fleet_shadow.h/.cpp widened to every level, people_renderer.cpp update; who else: RowKeeper's rows, agent_cost. Test: the lab's stage weights at the street view (shadow passes), agent_cost draws, traffic and people photos by day with shadows whole.

title: The plays texture is rebuilt as an Image and sent whole every frame, and its array is copied on…
symptom: The plays texture is rebuilt as an Image and sent whole every frame, and its array is copied on the next write. (An allocation and a texture upload a frame (small; P-08).)
cause: The rows are refilled from scratch each frame and the texture has no partial update path.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: a photo or a test of the place

title: Each frame the parked cars of a 5 x 5 block of cells vehicle_r_ (900 m) wide round the camera are…
symptom: Each frame the parked cars of a 5 x 5 block of cells vehicle_r_ (900 m) wide round the camera are gathered into one list and sorted, then each is distance-tested: the cars of some 20 square kilometres for a disc of 2.5. (Main-thread time every frame growing with the parked cars of the district, not with those in reach.)
cause: The cell of the parked index is as wide as the whole publish radius and the gather takes a margin cell each side; the list is sorted every frame to keep the publication order.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: a photo or a test of the place

title: A far tree mesh is every tree of a 1024 m superchunk as a card, built by one job that walks the…
symptom: A far tree mesh is every tree of a 1024 m superchunk as a card, built by one job that walks the whole wood lattice of its 16 chunks (noise, grade and ground tests with a dozen height_at a candidate), every street tree and every lot garden, holding the map shared throughout (line 197); any road or building change in any of its chunks marks it and builds it all again (mark_dirty line 98, render_world.cpp:167-178). (Seconds of worker time after opening a city (every superchunk within far_m), repeated rebuilds while the city grows, and the map held shared for the length of each (stalls: P-02).)
cause: The far level unit of rebuild is the superchunk, placement is recomputed from scratch each time, and the job reads the map directly under the shared lock.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: The far cards' unit of rebuild is the chunk: TreeRenderer keeps each chunk's cards and a superchunk's mesh is joined from its sixteen parts, only the chunk marked placed again (mark_dirty marks the chunk; the far tier asks the superchunks holding a marked chunk). Placement reads the job's cut (P33), so the map is not held. Check: far tree photos equal, a probe counting chunks placed a far rebuild (one for one grown building), growth_pick_test.

title: A near tree chunk sends each species buffer to three MultiMeshes (body, shadow caster, cards): the…
symptom: A near tree chunk sends each species buffer to three MultiMeshes (body, shadow caster, cards): the same 80-byte rows three times on the GPU, each kept three more times on the CPU by the engine, and up to three instances a species a chunk. (Memory of the near trees about twelve times their rows (960 bytes a tree) and instance count (P-03).)
cause: Body, caster and cards are separate meshes drawn by separate MultiMeshes over the same instances.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: A species of a near chunk holds its rows once: the body and its caster are two instances of one MultiMesh (the caster the body mesh's shadow level, or a shadows-only instance of the same MultiMesh), the cards a level of the same mesh where the engine's level choice serves, so a tree's rows are not copied three times (with P13 and P19: rs_util.h MultiMeshDraw twin by instancing). Look up instancing a MultiMesh RID twice and shadow meshes in context7 first. Check: tree photos near and at the hand-over equal, MultiMesh count and bytes of render_cost lower.

title: Boot rasterises procedural assets on the CPU at every launch: the leaf atlas, every species tree…
symptom: Boot rasterises procedural assets on the CPU at every launch: the leaf atlas, every species tree pictures (a get_pixel engine call a covered pixel), the vehicle meshes with their simplified levels and wrecks, the bay props, the film LUT; and reads the 61 MiB people file and 22 MiB atlas. (A slow start of the game and of every test process (each test pays the whole boot).)
cause: Assets that never change between runs are made in code at startup instead of being cooked once to files.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: a photo or a test of the place

title: At any change of the land or the water (a road laid changes terrain rects: render_world.cpp:132…
symptom: At any change of the land or the water (a road laid changes terrain rects: render_world.cpp:132 touch) a job recomputes the shore levels of the whole map: a height_at for every water sample of the map inside one shared hold of the map lock, then the spread passes, then the whole raster is uploaded again. (A long shared hold of the map at each road or land edit and while roads grow (stalls: P-02), a worker busy and a full texture upload each time.)
cause: The shore field has one revision for the whole map and no region to redo; its job reads the map directly under the shared lock.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: C11: the shore field is worked by tile. ShoreField::touch takes the changed rects (RenderWorld::drain_log has them: terrain_rects and the water chunks) and marks the tiles whose samples the change can reach (the rect grown by terrain_shore_reach_m); the job copies a tile with that margin through cut_city with CUT_WATER (a GroundPatch) and spreads it alone; sync sends that tile's rows of the texture. Callers to check: render_world.cpp drain_log and full_rebuild (reset), render/shore_view.gd (grid and texture unchanged). Test: a shore probe after a terrain edit equal to a whole remake, and the shore photos. The C9 part now: the job's copy is taken through MapRead.

title: A new map (and the first raster) computes the ecology of every chunk of the map (compute_ecology…
symptom: A new map (and the first raster) computes the ecology of every chunk of the map (compute_ecology for some 6,100 chunks of a 20 km land) in one job, and every later job copies and re-uploads the whole raster; the trees and cover compute the same ecology again per chunk in chunk_ground. (A worker busy for the whole map after every open (tests included), the same work done twice, whole-texture uploads at each nature edit (cost of compute_ecology to total when sim/nature is read).)
cause: The ecology is rasterised for the whole map eagerly instead of for the view, and has two owners (the raster and ChunkGround).
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: C11: the ecology on the ground follows the view and has one owner. The raster becomes a window round the eye whose texels keep their place modulo the window (as FogField): only the chunks within the fine ground's reach are rasterised, each chunk's corners taken from the ChunkGround the trees and the cover keep (GroundKept: the one place compute_ecology runs for a chunk), sent by chunk rows. Callers to check: RenderWorld::sync_nature (touch), render/ecology_view.gd and terrain_ground.gdshaderinc (window instead of whole-map grid), full_rebuild. Test: the raster's texels equal the chunk ground's communities at sampled corners; after a new map no job walks the whole map (a probe of chunks computed). The C9 part now: each chunk's ecosystem is worked out from a cut, off the map lock.

title: The cover job (lattices of the chunk with ground, road and lot tests, and for a shore chunk every…
symptom: The cover job (lattices of the chunk with ground, road and lot tests, and for a shore chunk every water sample within search_m of each lattice cell with a height_at each) and the tree jobs hold the map shared for their whole build. (Longer shared holds of the map (P-02).)
cause: The same decision as the road jobs: jobs read CityState in place under the shared lock.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: CoverRenderer::submit and TreeRenderer::submit gather a CityCut of their chunk (far trees: of their superchunk) under the short lock: ground patch with water levels, nature (ground paint cover of the box, planted trees and clearings, elements of the chunks, ecology settings), the roads and lots near, the buildings' records for the gardens; build_chunk/tree_place/garden_place/chunk_ground read the cut. The shared_lock at cover_renderer.cpp:210 and tree_renderer.cpp:197 go. Check: map_hold_test (built_under_map 0 with trees and cover streamed), frozen photos byte-equal (trees and cover stand where they stood).

title: Tracks and stops are meshed on the main thread inside RenderWorld::sync, under the map shared…
symptom: Tracks and stops are meshed on the main thread inside RenderWorld::sync, under the map shared lock: geometry, height and road queries, create_mesh and instances, up to items_per_frame a frame; any road or terrain change under an item queues it again. (Hitches when rails are laid or the ground or roads under them change (only on maps with transit).)
cause: The transit renderer has no job path: its items are built where they are committed.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: TransitRenderer builds its items in jobs: sync() only gathers (a CityCut with the transit plan, the roads and ground under the item) and submits through a MeshQueue (lane TRANSIT, key the item's signature); transit_track_parts/transit_stop_parts fill MeshBuilders on a worker from the cut; the main thread adopts the baked meshes under the frame's admission. items_per_frame stops being a build budget. Check: transit tests (transit_test, rail photos), map_hold_test with a line laid.

title: With the congestion layer on, every refresh_s each road chunk in reach has its ribbon copied,…
symptom: With the congestion layer on, every refresh_s each road chunk in reach has its ribbon copied, coloured and made a new mesh on the main thread (mesh_of_arrays), the old one freed. (A periodic hitch while the congestion layer is shown.)
cause: The congestion colours are baked into vertex colours of a mesh made again each refresh instead of being data the shader reads.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: The congestion layer's colours become data the shader reads: a chunk's carriageway ribbons are one mesh made once by a job (lay_congestion from a CityCut), each vertex carrying its segment's slot in CUSTOM0; a small level texture (one texel a slot, the traffic's published flow) is updated each refresh_s with the texels that changed; overlay shader mixes the colour from the level. update_congestion makes no mesh. Look up RenderingServer texture update calls in context7 before coding. Check: overlay test/photo of the congestion layer equal in colour to before, no mesh_of_arrays in update_congestion.

title: Each agent of each publication reads and writes its wear cell through PackedByteArray calls into…
symptom: Each agent of each publication reads and writes its wear cell through PackedByteArray calls into the engine (operator[] and ptrw per add), and a sent tile is copied on its next write because the upload image shares its array. (Main-thread time each publication growing with the agents (small).)
cause: The wear tiles are engine arrays so they can be handed to the texture without a copy.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: a photo or a test of the place

title: The canyon window (512 x 512 cells of building tops) is made whole again each time the camera…
symptom: The canyon window (512 x 512 cells of building tops) is made whole again each time the camera moves an eighth of the window or any building chunk in it changes: every lot of the window through record_mass, two sliding-max passes, and a full texture upload. (A worker job and a texture upload every hundred metres or so of camera travel and at each building grown in view.)
cause: The window has no incremental path (the fog field beside it has one): a move or a change remakes all of it.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: C11: the canyon window is made incrementally. Texels keep their place modulo the window (the shader reads it repeating, as the fog's); a move of the view lays only the strips it entered and a changed building chunk only that chunk's cells (CanyonField::touch keeps the chunks, not one revision); the sliding maxima are redone for the rows and columns within reach of what changed; the upload is the changed rows. Callers to check: render_world.cpp drain_log (touch), render/sky_view.gd and atmosphere.gdshader (window read repeating), reset. Test: a canyon probe after moves and a grown building equal to a whole remake. The C9 part now: the job's copy of the records is taken through MapRead.

title: While any piece moves or burns (a wreck burns car_burn_s seconds without moving) Debris::flush…
symptom: While any piece moves or burns (a wreck burns car_burn_s seconds without moving) Debris::flush writes every piece again and sends each non-empty layer whole: multimesh_set_buffer of the full capacity (debris_max x 80 bytes a layer), not the rows that changed; Debris::add erases from the middle of a deque per piece once over debris_max. (Main-thread time and a full buffer copy per layer every frame after a blow for as long as wrecks burn; only while effects are live (not the idle city).)
cause: An effect layer is a MultiMesh of fixed capacity rewritten whole from the piece list (MmLayer::upload has no dirty range, and Godot's set_buffer takes the whole buffer); 'burning' counts as 'changed' although a burning piece at rest writes nothing new.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: a photo or a test of the place

title: The cut ruins are kept up to 6,000,000 vertices (the comment: about 170 MB) plus most_falls of…
symptom: The cut ruins are kept up to 6,000,000 vertices (the comment: about 170 MB) plus most_falls of them, each with its RuinMesh (pieces, links, the GPU mesh), its RuinSim, its rows, a float RGBA texture and a duplicated ShaderMaterial; a ruin at rest is still the whole cut building, and every ruin of a saved city is cut and settled again in a job at open (settle_most_steps rigid steps a ruin). (Memory (process and video) that grows with every building brought down and never returns below 170 MB worth of ruins; job time and a material/texture a ruin at open of a damaged city.)
cause: A fallen building stays drawn as its own cut walls for good (one mesh and one material a ruin) instead of being reduced to its heap once at rest; the budget is counted in vertices against a constant in the code, outside any memory budget of the game.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: a photo or a test of the place

title: The simulation thread takes map_mutex exclusively for each building that grows (apply_growth), for…
symptom: The simulation thread takes map_mutex exclusively for each building that grows (apply_growth), for each flow-control choice (line 81) and tries it exclusively every step for damage_step (line 91). Each exclusive take waits for every mesh job that holds the map shared for its whole build (P15), and while it waits libc++'s shared_mutex lets no new reader in: the frame's two or three shared takes (city_core.cpp:188,195; render_world.cpp:246) and every other job queue behind it. Each grown building also bumps the city revision (city_growth.cpp:117), which voids every cache keyed by it (P22, furniture_kept), and marks its building chunk, whose near meshes, superchunk far mesh (P5), trees near and far (P27) and lots_changed bays are made again. (While a city grows: frame stalls of the length of the longest running mesh job, at the growth rate; CPU on all workers rebuilding whole chunks and superchunks for one building; the damage clock running late.)
cause: The city's time-driven changes (growth, damage clock, signal choices) are applied in place on the one CityState every reader reads in place, so each needs every reader out; and a change is announced by chunk and by whole-city revision, not by the record that changed.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: Simulation::tick no longer holds map_mutex exclusively round the whole growth step: grow_step (city_growth.cpp) takes the map shared to decide each building and exclusively only to add it (port-from-nov7 P30). The damage step's try-lock stays as it is. Check Simulation::step (tests), hold_still. Test: growth scenes, state hash, map_hold.

title: Each building the growth adds makes LOOK_CANDIDATES whole generated bodies (b40::record_body, the…
symptom: Each building the growth adds makes LOOK_CANDIDATES whole generated bodies (b40::record_body, the full building body) through a blocking parallel_for on the job pool to keep the one least like its neighbours, plus the look of every building within LOOK_REACH_M (designs.made->look); fill_all does the same serially for every lot of the generated city at founding. pick_free walks every queued cell and lot (two grid queries a lot) once per building owed. (Simulation-thread time under the shared map lock at each grown building (the tick runs late: traffic stutters while the city grows); a slow new-city founding; body cache filled with bodies never drawn.)
cause: The choice between candidate seeds is made on complete bodies (walls, volumes, roofs) because the look is derived from the finished body, not from the plan's first stage; the candidates not kept still enter the body cache.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: growth's candidates and looks are read from the tables' BodyCache (record_body, BodyCache::look) under the SHARED map lock: grow_step decides one building beside the frame and takes the exclusive lock only to add it (port-from-nov7 P30); record_for and look_of take a const CityState; BuildingStore::looks goes. Check fill_all, city_core_park_probe look_of. Test: growth scenes, state hash, map_hold.

title: Every change of the lane graph (a road edit, and each automatic control choice applied by…
symptom: Every change of the lane graph (a road edit, and each automatic control choice applied by apply_flow_control through log.net_node) bumps lane_graph_serial, and the next traffic step rebuilds whole-map indexes on the simulation thread: the ring index (a bounded Dijkstra from every directed segment), the reach components (Tarjan over the whole segment graph, twice: route_reach.cpp:95), the router's per-segment targets, and the graph part of each of the three published views (traffic_view.cpp:24: tallies and junction views of every segment and node). (A late tick (traffic freezes for a moment) at each road edit and each time a junction changes control by itself, growing with the size of the network, not with the edit.)
cause: The traffic's derived indexes are keyed by one serial of the whole lane graph, although apply_network_changes knows exactly which nodes and segments changed (it rebuilds only those in the graph itself).
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: a photo or a test of the place

title: The simulation thread asks the whole generated body of a building (b40::record_body) for one…
symptom: The simulation thread asks the whole generated body of a building (b40::record_body) for one derived fact each time: the bays of every lot within park_window_m of the camera (read_lot), again with up to three grid searches of the lot for a bay's way out (parking_lanes.cpp:93), again for a yard (yard_input.cpp:107), the storeys and look of growth candidates (growth.cpp:119), a garden for every tree job (P28). The bodies come from one cache budgeted in megabytes (sim_body_cache_mb) shared with the render's near buildings. (Memory in the body cache well past the buildings in view, or, when the budget is under the working set, bodies generated again and again on the simulation thread and the workers (CPU, late ticks) as the camera moves.)
cause: A building has one derived form, the complete Body (volumes, walls, lot elements), and no smaller product for what the traffic and the trees need of a lot (its elements); every reader of a lot therefore pulls whole bodies through the same cache, so the cache holds or keeps re-making bodies of buildings that are never drawn near.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: read_lot (parking_sources.cpp:68), read_lots_with_docks (185), street_gates (lot_access.cpp) and road_markings already ask b40::record_elements, the lot's elements alone, not the whole body; what is left: the ways out (parking_lanes.cpp:93) and the yard (yard_input.cpp:107) still take record_body for the grid of volumes, and growth.cpp:119 for storeys and look. Fix: those readers take the derived products they need (the elements and the ground volumes' footprints) from BodyCache as their own keyed entries, never the whole body; check with the body cache's bytes probe in km24 while the camera moves.

title: A yard's fine search may expand 1,500,000 poses: its poses live in chunks of 65,536 WayNodes…
symptom: A yard's fine search may expand 1,500,000 poses: its poses live in chunks of 65,536 WayNodes (about 4 MiB a chunk, way_space.h:75), the comment counting 2.6 million poses for one (some 160 MiB), plus the heap's chunks, the pose tables' pages and a distance map of doubles per dock and grain (way_field.cpp:117), all on the simulation thread's heap for as long as the planner of that yard lives. (A transient of tens to hundreds of MiB and many ticks of planner work on the simulation thread when a lorry is first called to a works near the camera (memory peaks that mimalloc returns only after the thread's own later activity, P41).)
cause: The planner searches the lorry's way on a grid of place and heading over the whole lot and its streets at a quarter metre, keeping every pose it queued, and falls from the coarse grain to the fine one for a tight yard.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: a photo or a test of the place

title: In the uncommitted FinalHeights change of this session, every read of a final height (at) and…
symptom: In the uncommitted FinalHeights change of this session, every read of a final height (at) and every write (put) turns the flat sample index back into tile and offset with six integer divisions by runtime values (i % n_, i / n_, z / tile_, x / tile_, z % tile_, x % tile_); height_at reads four samples a call (grid_sample) and patch() one a sample of its window. (CPU in the hottest read of the core (every mesh job's ground heights, the effects' rigid bodies, parking, doors, the cursor's ray) if this change is committed as it stands: it trades 105 MiB of a 20 km land for time in every height read.)
cause: The tiled store kept the flat index of the whole-map array as its interface instead of taking (x, z) and a power-of-two tile side (a shift and a mask); the callers already hold x and z.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: Redone for the tree taken back to a1a771c4 (P18 of trace port-from-nov7): sim/terrain/final_heights.h FinalHeights owned by the Heightfield: 16-bit tiles of 64 x 64 samples made the first time a sample is set, the base elsewhere; column and row only (shift and mask); grid_sample hands (ix, iz); users: heightfield.cpp, compose.cpp, road_shape.cpp, height_patch.h, render/terrain_bridge.cpp, api/city_core_state_probe.cpp. Tests at the end: road_grade_test, save_undo_test, edit_fuzz_test, digest (golden moves with the stored form), photos of roads on slopes.

title: street_gates asks record_mass (the whole generated body of the lot, made if not cached) for every…
symptom: street_gates asks record_mass (the whole generated body of the lot, made if not cached) for every lot within reach of a street segment, only to read the positions of its EL_CAR_GATE elements; lot_access builds a 0.25 m grid over the whole lot and runs Dijkstra over it (twice with docks) for the ways of its bays. (CPU on the simulation and job threads at each street change and each parking lookup, bodies of never-drawn buildings made and held; memory churn in the body cache.)
cause: A lot's gates, bays and ways have no stored form of their own: every reader (kerb parking of a segment, the parking sources, the yard planner, the garden trees) re-derives them from the whole Body, which the 128 MB cache keeps or makes again (same decision as P45 and P28).
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: A lot's facts for the traffic are facets kept with its elements by the body's key (BodyCache): street_gates already reads the kept elements (3e3c48e2); the ways of lot_access (the 0.25 m grid and its Dijkstra) become a kept facet  (gates, bays with their ways), made once a lot and read by parking_sources, parking_lanes and yard_input, which no longer ask the whole body. Check: yard_test, traffic_hash_test, digest, the park_sample probe.

title: Every command ends (finish_command, under the exclusive map lock on the caller's thread) by…
symptom: Every command ends (finish_command, under the exclusive map lock on the caller's thread) by recomputing whole lot cells: LotCache::process_dirty cuts again every 256 m cell queued, each from a 496x496 raster (block_lots res 1 m: 246 KiB bytes + 984 KiB labels), a 248x248 strip grid, discs along every street within 160 m, and for each frontage step of each zoned side every design tried with unfit (ground lattice through std::function) and to_paving (three walks of every segment with closest_t). Cells are queued by RoadNetwork::mark_segment (160 m round any changed segment) and by mark_ground: any ground move (a relief dab, a road whose solved height moved in sync_grade) queues the lot cells of its box. The command then bumps the city revision (touch), which drops every cache kept by revision (P22, P48). (A hitch at each road edit, zone dab, undo/redo and relief stroke near streets: the frame's thread holds the map exclusive while cells are cut again (the simulation and every render job wait behind it), then the revision bump redoes furniture and kept meshes.)
cause: The proposed lots are derived per 256 m cell (plus a 120 m margin) as a pure function of all streets round it, and the derivation runs inside the command's exclusive section; the unit of recompute is the cell, not the street side or block that changed, and ground moves are treated as street changes.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: The proposed lots become derived per street side (the zoned frontage of one segment side), keyed by that side's inputs (its curve, profile, zone, the streets crossing its strip): a command marks the sides its change reaches, not 256 m cells round 160 m boxes; the derivation leaves the exclusive section (computed from a cut by a job and adopted, like the meshes); a ground move marks lots only where the paving under a side moved. Owners: sim/lots (LotCache), RoadNetwork::mark_segment's lot cells (road_network.cpp), road_edit.cpp mark_ground and finish_command. Check: a command's exclusive time in km24 (edit probe) before and after, and the lots' digest unchanged on a fresh city.

title: Opening a city (and founding a new one, city_gen.cpp:110) derives everything of the whole map…
symptom: Opening a city (and founding a new one, city_gen.cpp:110) derives everything of the whole map before it is ready: found_land generates the land of every height sample from the seed (Heightfield::fill), read_terrain recomposes the whole heightfield (line 49), grade.everything solves every road and shapes the ground to each, mark_all_lot_cells + process_dirty cut every 256 m cell of the map again (line 301), and a new map also runs fill_all (a whole generated body for every lot, serial, P43). None of it is kept: lots, composed heights, road heights and bodies are derived again at every open. (Slow opening and slow new city; every test that opens a map pays the whole derivation (the slow tests), with a transient of the whole land in memory on the opening thread.)
cause: The save keeps only what the player made and the seed; every derived layer (land, final heights, road grade, lots, bodies) is a function recomputed from scratch for the whole map at open, whatever the camera will see, instead of being stored or derived by region on demand.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: Every derived layer is derived by region where it is read, never for the whole map at open: the land of a region from the seed when the terrain bridge or a reader asks it (Heightfield by tiles, a tile filled on first read), the composed heights and the road grade per region as their roads come into reach (grade solved by the region's segments and their joints, the ground shaped to them there), the lots per 256 m cell when growth or the view needs the cell, the bodies already on demand (BodyCache); the save keeps what the player made, and an open only founds the regions the camera and the simulation's windows read. Who else: city_gen (new map: fill_all over the cells growth reads), CityCore::new_map/load, the traffic's lane graph (whole network, cheap), the lot sites. Test: open_probe on km24 (map 4) and the town before and after (the open's parts by ms), every core test's open time, the photos of a freshly opened city judged whole (P470 measures the same opening).

title: Every frame the camera settle asks the core map_revision, two raycasts straight down from ray_top…
symptom: Every frame the camera settle asks the core map_revision, two raycasts straight down from ray_top 20000 (focus and eye; a third while moving), sight_pull with 48 samples and eye_free (twice while moving): each takes map_mutex shared on the main thread, and sight_pull, eye_free and clear_reach gather the solids of the buildings in the box again per call (record_mass per building, vectors allocated: api/city_core_sight.cpp). CameraQueries keeps the answers only while the map revision holds, and touch() moves it at every command and every grown building (up to 25 a second), so a camera at rest over a growing city re-asks all of it every frame. (CPU on the main thread every frame; the frame waits whenever the simulation or a command holds or waits for the map exclusive: stutter while the city grows and while the camera moves.)
cause: The camera has no stored form of what it may collide with: every frame it re-derives the solids from the whole CityState under the map lock, and its cache is keyed by the whole-city revision (same decision as P22, P48); a main-thread reader of the map queues behind any waiting writer (P42, P51).
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: a photo or a test of the place

title: InteriorController._process asks interior_revision of the core every frame, and CityCamera asks…
symptom: InteriorController._process asks interior_revision of the core every frame, and CityCamera asks map_revision every frame: one integer each, read under map_mutex shared on the main thread. (Main-thread waits behind growth, commands and the simulation exclusive sections, every frame.)
cause: Revisions the scripts poll are fields of CityState guarded by the map lock instead of atomics published by the writer; the frame pays a lock (and queues behind a waiting writer) to learn that nothing changed.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: a photo or a test of the place

title: Every mouse motion event asks the core a raycast for the ground point (map shared lock) and then…
symptom: Every mouse motion event asks the core a raycast for the ground point (map shared lock) and then the tool in hand asks more: Inspect (the empty-hands tool) asks inspect at every move; the road tool asks road_end, road_pieces and preview_road_path and rebuilds the preview mesh; the Build tool with a part in hand asks body_pick (record_body of every record along the ray); the Lots tool asks lot_at, lot_snap_point and rebuilds every ribbon of every lot; a handle drag asks body_draft (whole body copied, edited, written to bytes, its ghost meshes made on the main thread). A held brush (zone, ground paint, trees, elements, fog, relief dab each dab_s) sends one command per pointer move: each is a run_edit under the exclusive map lock with finish_command (P51) and marks the snapshot stale, so the whole snapshot is read again the next frame. (The frame stalls while the pointer moves with a tool in hand and stutters along a brush stroke; worse while the city grows (the main thread queues behind the simulation's exclusive sections).)
cause: A tool has no local model of what it previews: every pointer move is answered by the core from the whole CityState under the map lock, and every dab of a stroke is a full command with the command close (lot cells, revision bump, cache drops) instead of the stroke closing once.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: Pointer motion is answered once a frame, not once an event: ToolController keeps the frame's last motion and asks the ground point and the tool's hover/drag in _process (one raycast and one preview a frame); the previews hold the map shared (port-from-nov7 P452 already moved preview_roundabout, segment_at and preview_lot off the exclusive hold). A brush stroke is one command: the dabs between begin_stroke and end_stroke append to the open journal entry without finish_command's close (lot cells, revision bump, cache drops, the snapshot marked stale), which runs once at end_stroke (native/src/api/edit_result.h run_edit, sim/commands journal; callers: zone, paint, tree, element, fog and terrain tools; the store's _mark). Test: a probe counting finish_command closes and snapshot rebuilds over a held stroke of 60 frames (one each) and raycasts per frame under a burst of motion events (at most one).

title: The air is one full-screen pass at the 3D resolution, every frame: for each ground pixel…
symptom: The air is one full-screen pass at the 3D resolution, every frame: for each ground pixel cloud_shade walks every placed cloud (up to 24: a sphere test, then 5 steps of the 7-puff heap with noise); cloud_bodies fills the spans of all 24, picks nearest-first by a selection of O(n2) per pixel, and marches 16 steps a cloud, each step a cloud_density plus two more heaps (7 puffs each) and noise reads; mist, painted fog and the canyon light are in the same pass. (GPU time every frame with clouds, mist or fog on the map, growing with pixels x clouds in view.)
cause: Clouds, their shadows and the fog are ray-marched per pixel at full resolution inside the forward pass with per-pixel sorting of the clouds, instead of a low-resolution or cached field the pass only reads (a cloud's shadow on the ground is a 2D function of the map, recomputed per pixel per frame).
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: a photo or a test of the place

title: Every vertex of every person with a mesh works out its own pose on the GPU: for each play of the…
symptom: Every vertex of every person with a mesh works out its own pose on the GPU: for each play of the figure (up to PEOPLE_PLAYS blended clips) and each of its four bones it fetches two frames of three matrix rows, each row two RGBA8 texels (16-bit fixed point split in byte pairs): 48 texel fetches a play, and again in every pass that draws the mesh (depth prepass, colour pass, each of the four sun cascades); what is held and the helmet repeat it for their bone. (GPU vertex time proportional to people in reach x vertices x plays x passes: the crowd costs most where the city is busiest.)
cause: The pose has no per-figure result: the palette holds every clip of every body as byte pairs (P1) and the blend of clips and frames is redone per vertex per pass instead of once per figure per frame into a small table of bone matrices the vertices read.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: a photo or a test of the place

title: The ground's fragment, which covers most of the screen, works its whole look out per pixel per…
symptom: The ground's fragment, which covers most of the screen, works its whole look out per pixel per frame: four control-map corners, the ecology map, the grass map two to four times with a value noise each, two straw noises, four macro-tone noises, two patch noises, two grain and two speckle textureGrads, a soil read, two or three normal reads, a pebble read made always, the shore's four fetches, then soil, rock strata and painted surfaces where they show: about twenty texture reads (most anisotropic) and eleven value noises of four integer hashes each on plain near grass. (GPU fragment time every frame in proportion to the screen the ground fills, on any map, before anything is built.)
cause: Terms that vary over metres to hundreds of metres (macro tone, straw patches, patch shade, the wander of the bands, the biome tint) are procedural noise evaluated per pixel instead of being read from a low-resolution map of the ground made when the land changes; every layer is read whether or not its weight is zero (the pebble read, the second grass read).
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: a photo or a test of the place

title: The sky shader reads POSITION (the eye's height, for the low band it draws only outside the…
symptom: The sky shader reads POSITION (the eye's height, for the low band it draws only outside the cubemap pass) and LIGHT0_DIRECTION, and takes eleven uniforms Daylight sets at every hour step. By the engine's rule (Godot docs, Sky.process_mode and sky shader reference) a sky shader that uses POSITION is processed in the real-time mode and its radiance cubemap is rendered and filtered again whenever the camera position changes, when a directional light changes and when any uniform changes; the Sky is made with radiance_size 128 (city_world.gd:135), which the real-time filter overrides to 256. (GPU time in every frame the camera moves (six cube faces and the filter chain), and at every light step of the day cycle.)
cause: The low band of the sky is made a function of the camera inside the sky shader although the radiance does not show it (AT_CUBEMAP_PASS skips it): the engine can only see that POSITION is used. Daylight.follow_view already works the same share out for the fog and could hand it over as one uniform set when it moves.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: Redone for the tree taken back to a1a771c4 (P17 of trace port-from-nov7): sky.gdshader reads no POSITION: its uniform low is the deep band's share at the eye's height; Daylight.follow_view (which already works that share out for the fog) sends low_sky x share to the sky material only when it differs; _set_sky no longer sets low, low_from_m, low_to_m. Check: the low band from street level and from above in the final photos; tests at the end with the rest.

title: The sun's four cascades are fitted to reach as far as a 60 m caster's shadow is one pixel long (up…
symptom: The sun's four cascades are fitted to reach as far as a 60 m caster's shadow is one pixel long (up to shadow_depth_max_m 8000 m; 1600 m at the start view) and the engine draws all four again every frame: every caster instance in each slice (a building chunk is up to 130 instances: P3; the people's vertex pose is redone per cascade: P59; trees, props, roads), with blended splits and a 4096 atlas at medium, 8192 at high and ultra. (GPU time and render-thread culling and draw submission every frame, growing with the city in the shadow reach; the largest fixed cost of a high view.)
cause: One shadow technique for every distance: the far slices, where the casters are standing buildings and the sun itself is moved only a texel at a time (daylight.gd follow_clock), are rendered whole each frame like the near one, and the caster set is the drawn set (per-chunk instances) instead of a coarse caster of its own for the far slices.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: Redone on the tree taken back to a1a771c4 as P37 of the trace port-from-nov7: the cascades' reach is what the view shows (where the picture's top edge meets the ground, two steps past, the fade starting where the picture ends; the rule's and the tier's reach with the horizon in it) and the first cascade never ends short of the nearest ground shown; project/render/sun_cascades.gd (class SunCascades, split from daylight.gd); test tests/core/shadow_reach_test; measured at km24 (shadow primitives 8.61 to 5.59 M at the centre). The far level's own caster and the agents' casting rows by sector stay open there.

title: The medium tier (what the tests and every mid GPU run) has msaa 1 and temporal 1:…
symptom: The medium tier (what the tests and every mid GPU run) has msaa 1 and temporal 1: QualityTier.apply turns MSAA off only for FSR2, so MSAA 2x and TAA run together; high and ultra add FSR2 at full resolution, SSIL, the occlusion pass, the contact pass and the atmosphere pass in the same frame, each a full-screen pass at the 3D resolution (pixel_ratio up to 2). (GPU fill cost per frame in proportion to resolution x passes, on every view, with an empty map too.)
cause: Antialiasing and screen-space effects are stacked per tier as independent switches; nothing owns the frame's full-screen budget, so every effect reads the depth and shades the whole picture on its own (occlusion, contact, canyon, clouds, SSIL, TAA or FSR2, SMAA fallback).
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: Redone on the tree taken back to a1a771c4 inside the trace port-from-nov7 (its P14 and the survey of light and graphics): what the tier's temporal filter has to resolve is told to its users by the tier itself (QualityTier.apply): the buildings' dissolve and the railings' coverage noise read a global dither_resolved and a frame-sequence clock; the mip bias and the anisotropy stay the tier's. Check: quality_test, building_light_test, photos on the low and medium tiers. Test: a look plan on each tier with the hand-over band in view.

title: Every core and end-to-end test is a Godot process of its own that boots the whole game (CityWorld…
symptom: Every core and end-to-end test is a Godot process of its own that boots the whole game (CityWorld with Terrain3D and every material, CityStore.boot with the whole catalog and every renderer's boot work: the people asset read whole, signature looks unpacked, kits and atlases made: P30) and then opens a whole map (heights regenerated and composed, grade, every lot cell, the whole lane graph: P52) before its first check, whatever it tests. (Slow tests and slow task runs: seconds of boot and map opening per test before any check, multiplied by the suite.)
cause: The test harness has one unit, the whole game on a whole map: the core cannot be booted without the renderers' assets nor a test given a small piece of land, so the fixed cost of the two is paid by each of the hundreds of test processes.
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: a photo or a test of the place

title: in the 24 km city (map 4, 457,714 buildings) the core's allocator holds 3.3 GiB committed (103…
symptom: in the 24 km city (map 4, 457,714 buildings) the core's allocator holds 3.3 GiB committed (103 segments; peak 4.4 GiB, 15.7 GiB purged while the city was made), the working set is 5.1 GB and the private bytes 7.4 GB, and memory_census names the owner of 0.5 GiB of it only (terrain 213, body cache 266, building records 40 MiB) (5 GB of memory for the big city before anybody drives or walks in it)

title: the core's allocator is built for this toolchain (clang, MinGW, a static library in a DLL) without…
symptom: the core's allocator is built for this toolchain (clang, MinGW, a static library in a DLL) without its load and thread-end hooks: prim.c registers them with MSVC pragmas the compiler ignores (the callbacks land in .rdata: llvm-nm shows _mi_tls_callback_pre and _post as R symbols, never in .CRT$XLB), so _mi_auto_process_init and _mi_thread_done never run. The allocator stays in its preloading state: every purge is a MEM_RESET and never a decommit (the statistics of the 24 km city: reset 17.0 GiB, purged 17.0 GiB, resets equal to purges), and the heap of a thread that ends is never abandoned nor freed (threads 23 at peak and now, none ever leaves). (memory: in the 24 km city the allocator holds 3.2 GiB committed for 2.0 GiB alive (the making of the city peaks at 4.5 GiB and nothing of the 17 GiB it freed is given back), and each save, opening and restart of the simulation leaves its thread's heap behind for the life of the process)
cause: the allocator was fetched and linked with its defaults, which hook the process only under MSVC or as a shared library; the build never checked that the hooks run
criterion: the symptom gone where the trace `performance-root-causes` found it, checked as it planned: native/CMakeLists.txt sets MI_WIN_USE_FLS (the allocator's own path for a static library outside MSVC: a constructor runs the process init, a fiber-local callback the thread's end); test first: tests/core/memory_test (a thread takes 256 MiB, frees them and ends: the allocator holds no more than a segment over what it held, and no thread more), failing before; then memory_probe on map 4: committed follows live; check job_pool_test, digest, the save and open tests (threads end there)

Whether that is the whole of photo 06 is for the retake to say (its town, seed 1, was not opened at this close: the street-level view of seed 7's corner, `09-close_street_level_day.png` of 19df2d88, draws everything); still to read: a storey filled with pillar bays, and the eye put exactly at a roof's height by `eye_free`. Again on 2026-11-12 in the set "plate" (cbdda94a): `03-plate_mid_day` (`[-47, -103, 25, 30, 40]`) shows a building's wall from near, the junction behind it. Read 2026-11-12 (`project/game/camera/camera_pull.gd`, `native/src/api/city_core_sight.cpp`, `data/game/camera.json`): the pull in front of a building is weighted by the zoom (`pull_full_half` 4.8 m, `pull_none_half` 19.2 m of half view): none past 19.2 m (the view at zoom 25 hidden by towers is the rig's rule there, as the reference's `pullWeight`), and between the two the eye is moved a SHARE of the way past what hides the target (`wanted * weight`), which is a place still behind it: at zoom 90 (half 6 m, weight 0.92) the eye stops 8 % short, before the wall it was to pass (`05-close_plate_a_day`). Again on 2026-11-12 in the set "garden2": `00-garden2_hedge_a_day` (the eye over a roof, the hedge behind it) and `04-garden2_planter_day` (the eye inside a structure)
criterion: from every view the player's rig allows, what stands in the state is drawn (a probe of drawn against state from street-level views; photos)

title: The fallen: the crawl, opened-belly and struck-part flags are sent and never drawn

title: Bodies go after 90 s: the gravely hurt vanish while still down, and one who bleeds out leaves nothing

title: A struck body falls from the idle clip's first frame, its lost limbs thrown as tinted cylinders

title: A shot at somebody on the ground aims at a straight capsule, not the body drawn; the dead cannot be shot

title: The ragdoll has no ankle or neck limits, no bone collision, no roofs and no joint friction
symptom: ragdoll.cpp holds knees and elbows only (hinge, 72-92); a foot swings round its shin and the head folds into the chest; particles alone meet the ground and walls (113-135), so a shin sinks over a kerb edge; off_walls skips anything above a wall's top (98), no roof holds a body; a body falls as a rag (no friction while it falls)
